title: I'm a beginner who got tired of aimless vibecoding. I built an open-source Godot 4 + AI Framework to get more efficient and focused development
author: jenkoshot23
selftext:
I'm a just getting into gamedev and have no background in computer science or gamedev at all, i work construction and play games in my free time and with the emergence of AI ive decided to get into game dev. It's been a lot of trial and error and tutorials and learning how to use AI. I’ve been using AI to help build my upcoming game, but I quickly ran into the same walls I think most hit when making games with AI: the AI maxes out its context limit trying to read 40 files just to change a speed variable, it hand-edits a .tscn file and breaks every UID reference, or it gets stuck in an endless loop of aimless vibecoding without making actual progress. Or maybe its just me because I lack the planning skills and technical knowledge to actually make a game.



To solve this, I built the Godot AI GameDev Framework. It’s a directory and playbook system designed to enforce structured tasks and constant forward motion. I’m currently using it to build my own game, and I've decided to open-source the entire framework (GPLv3 License).



It houses all of your projects it automatically creates a project with your design docs and the tools and markdowns ive made based on the tier of game you're making. It can also house all your mechanics ever made all your assets and more and then pull from those folders when making new mechanics and scenes in a new project. Check it out and the readme for more info.



You can grab it here: [https://github.com/Jenkoshot/Godot-AI-GameDev-Framework](https://github.com/Jenkoshot/Godot-AI-GameDev-Framework)



\*\*What this framework actually fixes:\*\*

I built this to solve four very specific failure modes that show up the moment you point an AI at a real Godot project:



\*   \*\*Fixes Aimless Vibecoding:\*\* Instead of open-ended chatting, the framework enforces a strict loop. It reads your design docs, reports a completion percentage, gives you exactly three structured tasks to choose from, and waits. You pick one, it writes a blueprint, and it executes. It ensures constant, forward motion instead of getting lost in the weeds.

\*   \*\*Fixes Scene Corruption:\*\* If you let an AI write directly to a .tscn file, it will eventually destroy it. This framework routes all Godot resource operations through a local Godot MCP Server. It talks to the engine directly—no raw file manipulation allowed.

\*   \*\*Fixes Context Bloat:\*\* An AI shouldn't need to read your combat math to fix an inventory bug. The framework uses tiered, lazy-loaded documentation. The agent only reads the exact system it was assigned to work on.

\*   \*\*Fixes Planner/Coder Collision:\*\* Asking one AI to design architecture and write code simultaneously usually results in bad architecture and bad code. This framework splits them into two distinct roles:

\*   \*\*The Architect:\*\* Reads the design docs, plans the system, and writes a detailed blueprint (scene tree, signal flow, export variables). Never writes GDScript.

\*   \*\*The Executor:\*\* Reads the blueprint, drives the MCP server, writes strictly-typed GDScript 4, and writes the tests. Never decides project scope.

\*   \*\*Fixes Reinventing the Wheel:\*\* Every project shouldn't have to rebuild a health bar. The framework includes a global shared library structure for mechanics, scenes, and assets that agents are explicitly mandated to check before they write new code.



\*\*A few other cool features:\*\*

\*   \*\*Adversarial Audits:\*\* After the Executor agent finishes writing code, the Architect agent runs an audit. It diffs the original blueprint against the code that actually landed to catch the coding agent silently dropping edge cases, and files bugs if it did.

\*   \*\*The Tweak Guide:\*\* Agents are forbidden from hardcoding magic numbers. Everything is exported and tracked in an auto-generated tweak\_guide.md file so you can tune your game's feel directly in the inspector without asking the AI where variables live.

\*   \*\*Procedural 3D Modeling:\*\* It integrates antics-modelkit. Instead of an AI hallucinating broken binary meshes, the agent writes deterministic JavaScript recipes to mathematically construct, dequantize, and load 3D models into a Godot test environment.



\*\*Setup & Requirements\*\*

It currently targets Godot 4.4+. You'll need Node.js (for the MCP server) and Python (for the sync scripts). I've tested it primarily on Windows using Claude Code, ChatGPT Codex, and Antigravity (Gemini).



Check out the README for the full setup guide and the exact workflow loop. I'd love to hear your feedback, feel free to fork it and iterate on it to make it your own, again I am no AI expert or experienced gamedev so any additions that makes it better or refines it is more than welcome

comments.author: Pilgrim_91
comments.body:
Thank you for your work! A lot of these problems can really be dodged if you double-check your every step with AI, but having it all available in one package will be a huge help both for beginners and advanced users.

And kudos for not being afraid to step into a new area of expertise.

comments.author: Spudly42
comments.body:
I've never had any issues with breaking IDs or really breaking anything, so maybe that's an issue with your MCP?

I do agree hierarchical memory and system definition details is helpful.  Using a kanban/task system where you groom them before hand can also be helpful, though I find it is mostly helpful for running autonomously overnight and does produce worse results in terms of excessive churn (insisting on testing and retesting).  I guess I kind of assume everyone just built their own bespoke versions of these.  There are a lot of custom things you'd end up wanting, like custom task drain jobs that spool up headless CLI runs to process your tasks.  I probably wouldn't want to try to get the working for any OS for example.

replies.author: jenkoshot23
replies.body:
Initially I had made base44 compile webapp to drop all my gd files into it then export it as pdf then paste into a chat ai like Gemini and ask it to fix x thing or paste my gdd with it to and add this feature, super non efficient, when I found out about clis and antigravity/claudecode/codex it made me feel very stupid for how I was trying to do it before, and me messing around with moving files inside my project made it break and I didn’t really have any know how or why it was happening.

Long story short I’ve learned a lot and this is just where I’m at and I thought I’d put it out there for people to check out and iterate on.

comments.author: 69Trash420Panda
comments.body: Ever hear of agent skills? Go find the ones for godot and combine it with godot-ai mcp. I’ve not had any of your issues in my pretty massive project.

replies.author: ZoraGaymer
replies.body: Take a look at the skills from The Divergent AI on Github -> [https://github.com/thedivergentai/gd-agentic-skills](https://github.com/thedivergentai/gd-agentic-skills) (Not mine). I've used them and they are actually really good. The recent "Godot Vision" addition also helps a lot.

comments.author: Stixx187um
comments.body:
Sounds in part like what I've been doing. Collaborator (chat side), Planner, and Builder for me. The most recent thing I'm summoning, I take a Collaborator prompt to Astra xHigh in Plan Mode. Collaborator and I review the plan, make revisions, then send to a Builder Astra xHigh. Review what Builder did during its pass with Collaborator, repeat, etc.

Just tossing conversational one-or-two shot prompts at Codex can be fun. But it won't get you much beyond a neat tech demo and a lot of wasted usage lol

replies.author: jenkoshot23
replies.body:
Yea the workflow I find is much easier to keep on track and efficient, you ask what’s the next task it evaluates based on design docs and project state and any bugs that are noted then creates top 3 most important tasks, creates a blueprint with all the files to touch and what to do then hands a prompt with model and effort level to send it to.

I find it works well as before I was kind of just asking it to add a feature that I thought was next or wanted to implement at the time and no true progress tracking or real order of operations. You can still do a custom task if you want though

Thanks for the comment:)
